items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Planted 20 turnip seeds in greenhouse bed A. Soil: bunker compost mixed with surface soil (tested safe). Depth: 1cm. Spacing: 10cm. Watered with treated cistern water. Temperature: 18C under grow lights.
items.expected_timeline: Germination 7-10 days. Harvest 45-60 days.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: 18 of 20 seeds germinated. 90 percent success rate. Seedlings are small but green. the_naive_son visited during school session and counted the seedlings. He said 18 was a good number.
items.expected_timeline: First true leaves in 14 days. Harvest still on track for day 55.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested 2.3 kg of oyster mushrooms from the inoculated acorn substrate logs. First successful mushroom crop. the_chef was present and immediately began recipe development. See recipe_dev_001 through recipe_dev_002.
items.expected_timeline: Second flush expected in 14 days from same substrate.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Planted 50 barley seeds from the seed vault source in greenhouse bed B. Soil: bunker compost. Depth: 2cm. Spacing: 5cm. Barley is a calorie crop. If successful, it will provide grain for porridge and flour.
items.expected_timeline: Germination 5-7 days. Harvest 90-120 days. This is a long-term crop.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested 12 turnips from Cycle 4 planting. Total weight: 3.8 kg. Average size: 320g. Smaller than pre-war varieties but edible. the_chef prepared turnip mash (see recipe_dev_004). The bunker ate fresh vegetables for the first time in 55 days.
items.expected_timeline: Cycle 5 planting scheduled day 60. Continuous harvest cycle established.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Second flush yielded 1.5 kg. Declining yield expected as substrate nutrients deplete. Inoculated 4 new substrate logs with spawn from the first culture. Expanding mushroom production to meet the_chef demand.
items.expected_timeline: New logs will produce first flush in 21 days. Continuous mushroom production now established.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested dried herbs: thyme, rosemary, and a wild nettle variety foraged by the_hunter from the surface. Total dried weight: 0.8 kg. Herbs are the most space-efficient crop. They provide flavour and trace nutrients. the_chef uses them in every recipe.
items.expected_timeline: Continuous harvest. Herbs regrow quickly under grow lights.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Planted 10 potato seed pieces from the expedition to The Allotments. Soil: bunker compost mixed with surface soil. Depth: 8cm. Spacing: 30cm. Potatoes are calorie-dense and store well. If successful, they will be the second major calorie crop after barley.
items.expected_timeline: Germination 14-21 days. Harvest 90-120 days. First bunker-grown potatoes expected day 155.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: 44 of 50 barley seeds germinated. 88 percent success rate. Seedlings are strong. the_naive_son measured the tallest seedling at 4cm. He is keeping a growth chart in his notebook.
items.expected_timeline: Tillering in 21 days. Head formation in 60 days. Harvest day 140-150.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Powdery mildew detected on 3 turnip plants in bed A. White powder on leaves. Isolated affected plants. Applied diluted vinegar solution (the_chemist formulation). Increased airflow by repositioning grow light baffles.
items.expected_timeline: Treatment should resolve in 7 days. Monitor for spread. If contained, no crop loss expected.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Powdery mildew resolved. No spread beyond the 3 initial plants. Those 3 were smaller but still edible. Harvested Cycle 5 turnips: 15 turnips, 4.2 kg total. Yield increasing with each cycle. the_chef now has a reliable turnip supply.
items.expected_timeline: Cycle 6 planting day 80. Yield trend: 3.8 kg, then 4.2 kg. Projecting 5 kg by Cycle 8.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Original substrate logs exhausted after 3 flushes. Total yield: 5.1 kg over 30 days. New logs (inoculated day 58) producing first flush: 1.8 kg. Mushroom production is now the most reliable protein source in the bunker.
items.expected_timeline: New logs will produce 2-3 flushes over 30 days. Continuous cycle maintained.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested 0.5 kg of honey from the bee colony (3000 bees, foraging on surface flora). the_botanist tested radiation: 12 Bq/kg, well below concern threshold. The honey is safe. It is the first sweetener produced in the bunker. the_chef used it for the Asha celebration cake (recipe_dev_018).
items.expected_timeline: Bees forage actively in spring. Next harvest projected day 100, estimated 0.8 kg.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Assessed 17 seed vault ampoules. 12 viable, 3 uncertain, 2 failed. Planted viable seeds: turnip (already growing), barley (already growing), potato (already growing), beans (2 varieties), cabbage, carrot, onion, radish, pea, lentil, squash. Plus wheat, rye, sunflower from second recovery. Total new plantings: 11 crop types.
items.expected_timeline: Fast crops (radish, lettuce): 30 days. Medium (beans, pea): 60 days. Slow (cabbage, squash): 90 days. Wheat and rye: 120 days.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: 8 of 10 potato seed pieces sprouted. 80 percent success. Shoots visible at soil surface. the_child_soldier asked if potatoes could grow in the dark. the_botanist said no, they need the grow lights. the_child_soldier said that was a tactical vulnerability. the_botanist agreed.
items.expected_timeline: First tubers forming underground. Harvest day 155-165.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested first lentil crop: 1.2 kg dried. the_chef prepared lentil stew (recipe_dev_019). Lentils are the highest protein crop in the greenhouse. They also fix nitrogen in the soil, improving conditions for other crops. the_quartermaster says lentils are the most important thing the greenhouse has produced.
items.expected_timeline: Second planting day 95. Continuous lentil cycle established.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested first radish crop: 2.1 kg. 30-day growth cycle. Radishes are the fastest crop in the greenhouse. They provide quick calories and the greens are edible. the_chef added radish greens to the nettle soup.
items.expected_timeline: Continuous radish planting every 15 days for staggered harvest.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Quarterly greenhouse yield summary. Total production: turnips 12.2 kg, barley (green, not yet harvested), mushrooms 6.9 kg, herbs 1.6 kg, potatoes (growing), lentils 1.2 kg, radishes 2.1 kg, honey 0.5 kg. Total caloric value: approximately 44,600 kcal. This represents 7 percent of bunker monthly caloric needs. Projection at full seed vault integration: 15 percent by month 4.
items.expected_timeline: Greenhouse capacity expanding. Seed vault ampoules will add 11 new crop types over the next 90 days. Target: 20 percent caloric self-sufficiency by month 6.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested both bean varieties from the seed vault. Variety 1: 1.8 kg dried. Variety 2: 1.4 kg fresh (shell beans). Total protein contribution is significant. the_chef is experimenting with bean stews. the_surgeon says beans plus barley is a complete protein.
items.expected_timeline: Second bean planting day 110. Continuous bean cycle.

items.author: the_botanist
items.details: Harvested first cabbage: 3 heads, total 2.8 kg. 90-day growth cycle. Cabbage stores well and provides vitamin C. the_chef says cabbage plus salt from the Salt Freeholders means coleslaw. The bunker is approaching culinary diversity that was unimaginable on day 1.
items.expected_timeline: Second cabbage planting day 115. With 6 crop types now producing, the greenhouse is feeding the bunker in meaningful quantities.
